stem: In a declarative language, the programmer

options.content: states what result is wanted, using facts, rules or queries
options.rationale: The language system decides how to find it.

options.content: lists every machine operation in order
options.rationale: That describes low-level code.

options.content: organises the program into classes and objects
options.rationale: That describes object-oriented programming.

options.content: controls which registers hold the data
options.rationale: That is low-level programming.

explanation: Declarative programs describe the result, not the steps.

stem: Which statement describes an imperative (procedural) language?

options.content: A program is a sequence of statements that change the state of the program
options.rationale: The programmer states how the result is obtained.

options.content: A program is made of facts and rules that are matched against a goal
options.rationale: That describes a declarative logic language.

options.content: A program is made of instructions for one particular processor only
options.rationale: That describes a low-level language.

options.content: A program is made only of classes with no statements
options.rationale: Object-oriented programs still contain statements.

explanation: Imperative code is a series of statements executed in order.

stem: Why is assembly language called a low-level language?

options.content: Each instruction becomes one machine-code instruction
options.rationale: It is close to the hardware.

options.content: It is easy to read because it uses English sentences
options.rationale: Assembly uses short mnemonics, not sentences.

options.content: It can run on any processor without change
options.rationale: Assembly is specific to one processor type.

options.content: It needs no translator
options.rationale: An assembler is needed.

explanation: Assembly is close to the hardware and specific to one processor.

stem: A programmer must write the firmware for a small controller with very little memory that switches a relay on a borehole pump. Which paradigm is the most suitable?

options.content: Declarative
options.rationale: The controller needs exact control of the hardware, not a query.

options.content: Object-oriented with a large class library
options.rationale: A large library would not fit the available memory.

options.content: Imperative, using many large libraries
options.rationale: Large libraries would not fit in the small memory.

options.content: Low-level
options.rationale: Direct control of the hardware and a small, fast program are needed.

explanation: Small memory and direct hardware control suggest low-level code.
hints: Which paradigm gives the programmer control of the hardware?

stem: A school wants one system with learners, teachers, classes and rooms, each with their own data and actions, and the types interact in many ways. Which paradigm suits this best?

options.content: Low-level
options.rationale: A large system of interacting types would be very hard to write in assembly.

options.content: Declarative only
options.rationale: A declarative language answers queries; it is not used to model objects with actions.

options.content: Object-oriented
options.rationale: Each type of thing becomes a class with its own data and methods.

options.content: Imperative, with one long list of statements and no routines
options.rationale: A single list of statements would be hard to manage for so many interacting parts.

explanation: Many interacting kinds of thing suggest classes and objects.
hints: Which paradigm combines data and actions in one unit?

stem: SQL is designed for one kind of task, working with databases. What type of language is it?

options.content: A general-purpose, low-level language
options.rationale: SQL is not low-level or general-purpose.

options.content: An object-oriented machine code
options.rationale: SQL is not machine code.

options.content: An imperative, assembly language
options.rationale: SQL is not assembly.

options.content: A special-purpose, declarative language
options.rationale: It is designed for one task and states what data is wanted.

explanation: SQL states what data is wanted, and is made for databases only.

stem: Which pair of statements about the paradigms is correct?

options.content: Every language belongs to exactly one paradigm
options.rationale: Many languages support several.

options.content: Python supports both imperative and object-oriented styles
options.rationale: A language can support more than one paradigm.

options.content: Assembly language can be moved to any computer unchanged
options.rationale: Assembly is specific to a processor.

options.content: Declarative programs are always faster than imperative ones
options.rationale: Speed depends on the problem and the system.

explanation: Languages and paradigms are not the same thing: one language can support several paradigms.
hints: Is a paradigm a property of a language or of a style of programming?

stem: Which is a general-purpose high-level language?

options.content: SQL
options.rationale: SQL is a special-purpose language for databases.

options.content: Machine code
options.rationale: Machine code is low-level.

options.content: Python
options.rationale: It is used for many kinds of problem.

options.content: Assembly language
options.rationale: Assembly is low-level.

explanation: A general-purpose language is not limited to one kind of task.

stem: A program written in a low-level language can usually be run unchanged on any type of processor.
explanation: False. Low-level code is written for the instruction set of one type of processor.

stem: In an object-oriented program, the data and the methods that act on it are combined in a single unit called an object.
explanation: True. An object holds its own data (properties) and the methods that work on it.

stem:

| Client | Days | Town |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|

| Mpofu | 8 | Mutare |

| Phiri | 5 | Gweru |

stem: State the name of the paradigm in which a program is built from classes and objects.
explanation: The object-oriented paradigm.

left.content: A set of queries over a database of patients
Firmware for a pump controller with very little memory
A calculation script that processes a list of marks step by step
A game with many kinds of character that interact

stem: Describe the difference between an imperative language and a declarative language. [2]

points.description: In an imperative language the programmer writes the statements that say how the result is obtained, step by step
In a declarative language the programmer states what result is wanted (facts, rules or a query) and the system decides how

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An imperative program is a sequence of statements telling the computer how to get the result. A declarative program states what result is wanted and the language system works out how.

explanation: How versus what.

stem: Describe two characteristics of a low-level language. [3]

points.description: It is specific to one type of processor (not portable)
Each instruction corresponds to one machine-code instruction and gives direct control of the registers and memory
It is harder to write and read than a high-level language (or produces fast, small programs)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Low-level code is specific to one type of processor. Each instruction matches one machine-code operation, giving direct control of registers and memory, but it is harder to write and read.

explanation: Close to the hardware.
hints: Think about the processor and the translator.

stem: A company is developing a booking system for a bus service with passengers, buses, routes and tickets, which are linked in many ways. Justify the choice of the object-oriented paradigm. [4]

points.description: Names the object-oriented paradigm
Each type of thing (passenger, bus, route, ticket) can be a class with its own data and methods
Objects can interact by calling methods, which models the links between them
Classes can be reused and extended (inheritance), and the system is easier to maintain in parts

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each kind of thing (passenger, bus, route, ticket) can be a class holding its own data and methods. Objects interact through methods, which matches the links in the problem, and classes can be reused and extended, so a large system is easier to maintain.

explanation: Link the paradigm to the problem.
hints: Name the paradigm, then link two features of the problem to its strengths.

stem: A manager wants to find all customers whose balance is below zero. Explain why a declarative language such as SQL is suitable for this. [3]

points.description: The data is stored in a database table
The manager only has to state what is wanted (customers where the balance is below zero), not how to search
The database system chooses the method of finding the rows

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The data is held in a table. In SQL the manager states only what is wanted, customers whose balance is below zero, and the database system decides how to search the table.

explanation: A query states the result wanted.
hints: Consider a query over stored data.

stem:
A clinic in Bulawayo wants to know how many older patients are in Ward A. Its data is in this table.

| Name | Age | Ward |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Moyo | 72 | A |
| Ncube | 34 | B |
| Banda | 65 | A |
| Chuma | 41 | B |
| Dube | 80 | A |

The question is answered in two ways.

**Method 1**

```
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM Patients WHERE Age >= 60 AND Ward = 'A';
```

**Method 2**

```python
patients = [("Moyo", 72, "A"), ("Ncube", 34, "B"), ("Banda", 65, "A"), ("Chuma", 41, "B"), ("Dube", 80, "A")]
total = 0
for name, age, ward in patients:
    if age >= 60 and ward == "A":
        total = total + 1
print(total)
```

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which method uses a declarative language?

options.content: Method 2
options.rationale: Method 2 gives the steps to follow.

options.content: Method 1
options.rationale: The query states what is wanted.

options.content: Both methods
options.rationale: Only the query is declarative.

options.content: Neither method
options.rationale: SQL is declarative.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the value produced by both methods.
parts.workedSolution: Moyo (72), Banda (65) and Dube (80) are in Ward A and aged 60 or over.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain the difference between the two methods in terms of the programmer's task.

points.description: In Method 1 the programmer states what is wanted (the count of patients meeting the condition) and the database system works out how
In Method 2 the programmer writes each step: a loop, a test and a counter

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: In Method 1 the programmer states only what is wanted and the database decides how. In Method 2 the programmer writes each step: the loop, the test and the counter.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give one reason why Method 2 might still be chosen by a programmer.

points.description: The data is not in a database (it is in a list in the program)
Method 2 can be combined with other processing in a general-purpose program, e.g. output or calculations that SQL does not do

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The data is already held in a list in the program, and the loop can be combined with other processing in the same general-purpose program.

parts.explanation: A general-purpose language can do more than one job.

explanation: The same question answered declaratively and imperatively.
hints: Read the table before the query.
Compare the loop with the query.

stem: A software company in Harare is working on three projects: (1) firmware for a solar-panel controller with a very small memory; (2) a graphical game with many different characters, items and places that interact; (3) a system for a hospital that answers questions asked of its stored records.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each project to the most suitable paradigm.
parts.explanation: Hardware control, interacting objects, and queries over stored records.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Justify your choice of paradigm for Project 2.

points.description: The characters, items and places can each be a class with data and methods
Objects interact by calling each other's methods, as in the game
Classes can be extended (for example a new type of character) without rewriting the rest

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each character, item and place can be a class with its own data and methods. Objects interact by calling methods, as in the game, and a new type of character can be added by extending a class.

parts.explanation: Link the problem to the paradigm.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which is a disadvantage of using the paradigm chosen for Project 1?

options.content: Programs cannot control hardware directly
options.rationale: They control hardware directly.

options.content: Programs need a compiler for a high-level language
options.rationale: Low-level code uses an assembler.

options.content: Programs are tied to one type of processor
options.rationale: Low-level code is not portable.

options.content: Programs cannot be stored in memory
options.rationale: They are stored in memory like all programs.

parts.explanation: A low-level program must be rewritten for a different processor.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State one reason why a general-purpose language could not replace the language chosen for Project 3.

points.description: A declarative query language answers questions about stored data without the programmer writing the search steps

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A declarative language lets the staff state what they want without writing the search steps.

explanation: Choosing and justifying paradigms for described problems.
hints: Name the paradigm first, then the feature of the problem that suits it.
